title: Microsoft Moves AI Governance From Policy to Runtime Enforcement
gist: Microsoft has published an AI governance architecture that relocates governance from written policy into runtime enforcement, continuous evaluation, observability and audit evidence, spanning nine domains and four functions (policy, control, visibility, proof). The concrete control plane is Microsoft Foundry's AI Gateway plus Purview, Entra ID, Defender and Azure API Management, with the gateway able to govern MCP tools without modifying MCP servers or agent code.

themes.theme: Governance as a Runtime Loop, Not a Document

insights.claim: Microsoft frames AI governance as a continuous operational loop in which policies set requirements, controls translate them into access and runtime rules, observability captures behaviour, evaluations test quality and safety, and audit converts telemetry into compliance evidence.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A reusable five-stage template for assessing whether an enterprise AI deployment is actually governed or merely documented — and for scoring competing vendor offerings.
insights.quote: The architecture treats governance as a continuous operational loop.
insights.locator: Microsoft has outlined an AI governance architecture

insights.claim: The stated operational test is that a written AI policy does not count as governance until the production system can demonstrate its enforcement.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A one-line audit question that will increasingly be asked in enterprise procurement and by regulators — vendors without runtime proof artifacts fail it.
insights.quote: Your AI policy is not governance until production can prove it.
insights.locator: Anthony Bartolo, Principal Cloud Advocate at Microsoft

insights.claim: Microsoft decomposes AI governance into nine domains — policy, data governance, model governance, observability, evaluations, security, identity and access, audit and compliance, and agent governance — with agent governance carved out as its own category.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Agent governance emerging as a distinct domain rather than a subset of model governance signals a separate budget line and a new vendor category.
insights.quote: Microsoft identifies nine governance domains: policy, data governance, model governance, observability, evaluations, security, identity and access, audit and compliance, and agent governance.

insights.claim: Organizations moving AI workloads into production are re-architecting their foundational structures rather than bolting governance on afterwards.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Implies a platform re-engineering cycle — and associated spend — that follows rather than precedes AI pilot deployment.
insights.quote: Organizations cannot scale what you cannot control
insights.locator: Manasa T. Ramalinga, Cloud Solution Architect at Microsoft

insights.claim: Microsoft Foundry's AI Gateway acts as the runtime boundary enforcing authentication, token limits, quotas and policy, making the gateway rather than the application the point of control.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The API gateway pattern is being reused as the AI control plane, which favours incumbents with existing gateway estates over point AI-governance startups.
insights.quote: Foundry's AI Gateway provides a runtime boundary for authentication, token limits, quotas, and policy enforcement.

insights.claim: The gateway can govern MCP tools — centralized authentication, rate limiting, IP restrictions and audit logging — without modifying MCP servers or agent code, making governance retrofittable onto existing agent deployments.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Zero-code-change retrofit is the adoption unlock for enterprises with sprawling MCP deployments; it also makes governance a network-layer sale rather than an application-layer one.
insights.quote: providing centralized authentication, rate limiting, IP restrictions, and audit logging without modifying MCP servers or agent code

insights.claim: Runtime controls are scoped to span interactions among users, agents, models, tools, APIs, MCP servers and enterprise systems — treating the whole agent call graph, not just the model call, as the governed surface.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Governance scope is expanding from model I/O to tool invocation chains, which is where the real enterprise risk sits and where telemetry gaps currently exist.
insights.quote: Runtime controls can span interactions among users, agents, models, tools, APIs, MCP servers, and enterprise systems.

insights.claim: Microsoft positions evaluations on both sides of deployment — assessing quality and safety against datasets before release using built-in and custom evaluators, then monitoring production behaviour afterward.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Continuous production evaluation, not just pre-release testing, is becoming the enterprise standard — consistent with practitioner reports of evals consuming a large share of AI engineering effort.
insights.quote: Evaluations are positioned both before deployment and in production.
insights.locator: Evaluations are positioned both before deployment

insights.claim: Microsoft's open-source Agent Governance Toolkit supplies runtime security for autonomous agents including policy enforcement and interception points, extending governance to agent identity, access, activity and workflow checkpoints.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing the toolkit is a standards land-grab: adoption of Microsoft's interception model would anchor enterprise agent governance to Azure primitives.
insights.quote: Microsoft's open-source Agent Governance Toolkit provides runtime security capabilities for autonomous agents, including policy enforcement and interception points.
insights.locator: Agent governance adds controls around agent identity

insights.claim: The Agent Control Specification defines checkpoints across agent inputs, model calls, tool execution and outputs, with higher-impact actions able to require human approval.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Risk-tiered human-in-the-loop gating is converging as the cross-vendor pattern for agent autonomy — the same shape as Cloudflare's destructive-action approvals.
insights.quote: as a mechanism for checkpoints across agent inputs, model calls, tool execution, and outputs, with higher-impact actions able to require human approval
insights.locator: Agent governance adds controls around agent identity

insights.claim: Microsoft maps its architecture onto the vendor-neutral NIST AI Risk Management Framework and Generative AI Profile, translating those governance concerns into concrete platform controls and telemetry.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: NIST alignment is the compliance bridge that makes this architecture defensible to auditors — and a template competitors will have to match rather than replace.
insights.quote: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework and Generative AI Profile provide a vendor-neutral framework for managing AI risks across the lifecycle
insights.locator: The approach is broader than a Microsoft-specific control plane.
